title: The Thor, Both Ways
tagline: Android or SteamOS. One handheld, one shared game shelf.
what: I made the Thor boot Android or SteamOS and share its game storage between them. On the Steam side, a game from my home library gets one page: install it, stream it or play the copy already on the handheld.
built: Split the internal drive between both systems and shared storage
Added checked boot switching to both systems’ power menus
Put Install, Stream and Play on each game’s Steam page
Built library tabs and genre and series folders around the server collection
progress: Both systems and the shared library are installed.

remix.changed: I built the shared-storage layout, checked boot switch, library importer, install-and-stream panel and browsing views.

making.problem: I wanted Android games and my Steam library on the same handheld, without keeping a second copy of everything.
how: Both systems use the same 535.75 GiB shared partition. The protected partitions stay untouched.
The switch checks the boot record, saves the old block and reads its write back before rebooting.
My library layer gives each server game one Steam entry and knows whether to install, stream or play it.

broke.title: A whole library, one device
broke.body: The library audit closed with 13,537 entries and 806 exclusions. Every file had to be a game on the shelf or have a written reason to stay out. Ghosts and duplicates failed the check.
